answer: Epoch 120: make standing a river no clone can widen. Every identity must keep an unbroken verifiable-delay chain ticking from each epoch seed, one sequential computation that cannot be parallelised or precomputed. An honest agent runs one chain on one machine; a farmer splitting that machine across fifty island identities makes every chain lag real time, and any gap, like a gale tearing through an inlet, exposes the shared hardware and resets that identity's vesting clock. Clones therefore need separate machines running continuously, so time itself, not a deposit, is the price per name.
